title: Token Pulse: throughput & p95 variance harness for core models
creator: Ethan Zhao
description: Build and maintain a tokens-per-second microbenchmark harness focused on capturing burstiness and p95 variance across our core models. The goal is a portable, CI-friendly runner that: 1) emits steady-state and microburst traffic shapes, 2) captures per-request latency and p95 stats, 3) produces deterministic baselines per-model+config, and 4) integrates with existing regression detectors and Grafana dashboards. This ticket covers design, implementation, CI integration, and dashboarding for the initial set of core models (redwood-7b, rw-13b, open-xxl). Important constraints: minimal test noise from infra (controlled GPU warmup and cache priming), repeatable synthetic prompts, and low overhead metric collection so the harness itself doesn't perturb throughput results.
comments: 2025-01-18 - Triage: scoped to core models list from product; agreed to prioritize a harness that runs in CI and locally. Owner assigned to Priya.

2025-01-22 - Design decision: implement in Go for lightweight concurrency and stable timer semantics. Rationale: lower jitter under high concurrency vs Python asyncio in our stress tests. Trade-off: smaller contributor pool vs better signal-to-noise.

2025-01-25 - Probe design: include three traffic shapes (steady-state, microburst 50-200ms inter-arrival, and ramp-step). Add KV-cache priming mode that runs N short inferences to simulate warm cache before measurement.

2025-01-29 - Metrics contract: export Prometheus metrics (tps_counter, latency_histogram, p95_gauge, error_rate) and push JSON artifacts to CI for regression checks. Baselines stored in S3 path s3://redwood-perf/baselines/token-pulse/.
2025-01-31 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/4512 (initial Go harness + steady-state runner). Requested review from runtime infra and telemetry.

2025-02-02 - Review notes: telemetry team asks to reduce metric cardinality (drop per-sequence-length labels in histogram) and to add a lightweight checksum to synthetic prompts to ensure stable input across runs. Updated PR accordingly.

2025-02-02 - Next: finish CI job that runs the harness nightly and on runtime-release branches, wire failure signal to perf-regression-alerting pipeline, and create Grafana dashboard panels for p95 drift and TPS delta from baseline.
